entries.4724e9aa7fb7ebed: NISSIN FOODS HOLDINGS CO.,LTD. has its registered head office in Yodogawa-ku, Osaka, while its actual business operations are conducted in Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo. In October 2008 it transitioned to a holding company structure and adopted its current trade name, and at the same time established Nissin Foods Co., Ltd., Nissin Foods Chilled Co., Ltd., Nissin Foods Frozen Co., Ltd. and Nissin Foods Business Support Co., Ltd. through a new company split. (instant noodles), Nissin Foods Chilled Co., Ltd., Nissin Foods Frozen Co., Ltd. and Nissin Yoke Co., Ltd. (low-temperature and beverages), and Koikeya Inc., Nissin Cisco Co., Ltd., Bonchi Co., Ltd., Seria Co., Ltd. and Royl (confectionery), among others; overseas, they include Nissin Foods(U.S.A.)Co.,Inc. (United States), Nissin Foods Brasil Ltda. (Brazil), Nissin Foods Company Limited (Hong Kong, listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange), Nissin Foods Kft. (Hungary) and Indo Nissin Foods PRIVATE LTD., among others. Equity-method associates include Thai President Foods Pub.Co.,Ltd., Marben Food Holdings Ltd., Nissin-Universal Robina CORP. and Premier Foods plc of the United Kingdom; the equity-method investment income for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥12,949 million.

The company states that in the domestic instant noodle business, the Nissin Foods segment achieved higher revenue as strong key brands, price revisions and initiatives for anniversary campaigns succeeded in expanding volume share, while the Myojo Foods segment also achieved higher revenue on strong key brands; in the domestic non-instant noodle business, revenue increased, led by the frozen business of the Low-Temperature & Beverage Business segment and by Koikeya Inc. and Nissin Cisco Co., Ltd. in the Confectionery Business segment; and in the overseas business, revenue decreased due to lower sales volume in the U.S. business and higher sales promotion expenses, among other factors. entries.5bcb16c21a089e6c: This segment is where Myojo Foods Co., Ltd. mainly manufactures and sells instant bagged noodles and cup noodles. The company's group has two instant noodle operating companies, Nissin Foods Co., Ltd. and Myojo Foods Co., Ltd., which are listed as separate reportable segments. The company holds 45.12% of the voting rights in it; although it does not hold a majority, it judged that a de facto controlling relationship exists, taking into account the dispersion of voting rights and past voting patterns at shareholders’ meetings, and consolidates it. entries.d05684a780602ff3: The Group uses an indicator called 'Core Operating Profit from Existing Businesses'. This is operating profit less the profit or loss of new businesses and 'Other income and expenses' as non-recurring profit or loss; its purpose is to measure the substantive growth of existing businesses by separating out the profit or loss of new businesses for which active and continuous up-front investment is planned. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, Core Operating Profit from Existing Businesses decreased 15.5% year on year to ¥70,602 million, operating profit decreased 16.2% to ¥62,330 million, profit before tax decreased 15.3% to ¥65,081 million, and profit attributable to owners of the parent decreased 17.5% to ¥45,380 million. As reasons for the decline in profit, the company cites cost increases due to rising material prices, among others, in the domestic instant noodle and domestic non-instant noodle businesses, and in the overseas business, lower revenue in the U.S. business and a decrease in equity-method investment income, among others. Segment profit (on an operating profit basis) was ¥32,147 million for Nissin Foods, ¥10,568 million for the Americas region, ¥8,958 million for the China region, ¥7,721 million for the Low-Temperature & Beverage Business, ¥7,574 million for Other, ¥5,277 million for the Confectionery Business and ¥3,443 million for Myojo Foods; the total of ¥75,692 million is reduced by an adjustment of ¥13,362 million, which includes intersegment transaction eliminations and other items of ¥3,925 million and Group-related expenses of ¥9,436 million. Comparing Myojo Foods, which has the smallest revenue, with the China region, the China region's revenue is about 1.6 times larger and its segment profit is about 2.6 times larger.

entries.f2f8f93200a99e49: This segment manufactures and sells mainly instant bagged noodles and cup noodles in mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and other areas. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥74,945 million (up 2.0% year on year), and segment profit (operating profit basis) was ¥8,958 million (up 51.7%), the largest profit growth among the seven segments. The company cites the following: in mainland China, the revitalization of existing sales networks and expansion of sales channels into inland areas led to sales growth, mainly for the Chinese version of Cup Noodle “Hewei Dao” brand group and the bagged noodle brand “Demae Ichiban”; in Hong Kong, instant noodle consumption remained firm, centered on higher-priced new products, and catering sales grew due to an increase in inbound tourists; and, as reasons for the profit increase, in addition to higher revenue, the effect of impairment losses on fixed assets and others recorded in the previous fiscal year. The company states that it is pursuing expansion of sales areas, expansion of sales of higher-priced bagged noodles, multi-category expansion into frozen foods and confectionery, and strengthening of its wholesale business. At its core is Nissin Foods Company Limited, established in Tai Po, Hong Kong, in October 1984 (ownership of voting rights 72.1%; regional management company for China). It is listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, and the company recognizes significant non-controlling interests (ownership interest 27.95%). Its group's revenue is ¥78,144 million, and profit for the year is ¥6,783 million. Guangdong Shunde Nissin Foods Co., Ltd., Fujian Nissin Foods Co., Ltd., Zhuhai Jinhai'an Yongnan Food Co., Ltd., Zhejiang Nissin Foods Co., Ltd. and others are responsible for manufacturing. The number of employees is 3,764 (in addition, an average of 354 temporary employees during the year).
